question: Does the frozen self-adaptive deployment form, with recipes and the new-site starting interval selected on external development databases, pass robustly at untouched ICU sites without any local calibration study?

databases.SICdb: Salzburg Intensive Care database (PhysioNet), single site
databases.HiRID: HiRID (PhysioNet, Bern University Hospital), single site
databases.Emory: Emory University Hospital ICU: PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2019 training set B (open access), hospital system B per the Challenge paper; single site; used by a separate earlier model line, never by this deployment form (see prior_project_use)

prior_project_use: none: neither database is on this machine (checked 2026-10-20: no SICdb/HiRID files in ~/Downloads or the project). The v3 lockbox for these databases was never scored. Emory: NOT naive. The project used PhysioNet Challenge 2019 training sets A and B (pooled) on 2026-06-16/17 for a separate, earlier model line: general ICU JEPA pretraining with 6-hour forecasts compared against persistence on glucose, potassium, HCO3, pH, MAP and lactate (physionet2019_pretrain.py, PHYSIONET2019_PRETRAINING_FINDINGS.md), DKABody calibration (physionet2019_calibrate_dkabody.py) and DKA encoder transfer. Those results were seen by the researchers. The data were not used to fit, select or tune the current deployment form, its recipes, theta0 or its gates.
development_data_used_for_this_system: MIMIC-IV v4 (training), eICU harmonized, NWICU v4, Zigong v1.1 (selection of recipes and the starting multiplier; Zigong's v3 lockbox was scored on 2026-10-18 and it is development data since)

deployment_form.point_model: per-cell recipe from external_recipe_selection_dev_20261019.json (MPR 40, change hurdle 7 of 47 continuous cells), selected on eICU/NWICU/Zigong by the predeclared rule: most databases point-robust, ties to the simplest
deployment_form.persistence_fallback: cells with recipe 'persistence' (platelets@1h) output the current value without point correction, make no point claim, and are gated on the interval only
deployment_form.recipe_rule: osler_jepa.recipe_availability.deployable_recipe (treatment-context ridge -> measurement-pure ridge when the site records none of the permitted treatment features)
deployment_form.day_one_weighting: covariate-shift weights from the inputs of the first min(200, 25%) arriving stays (no labels)
deployment_form.interval: v2 quintile value-bin normalization (osler_jepa.interval_scale 'quintile') + DtACI meta rate 20, site and care-unit levels, new-site starting log multiplier theta0 = 0.15 (site_adaptive_dtaci_prior_dev_20261019.json, selected by leave-one-database-out)
deployment_form.network_sharing: multi-hospital deployments only: DtACI on the network stream (whole stays interleaved at random, each hospital's order kept); site level learned from every hospital, unit level keyed by hospital with step ratio 1.0, used after 20 resolved outcomes (site_adaptive_network_dev_20261020.json, adopted by a predeclared within-eICU two-fold hospital split: held-out 77 vs 73). Single-hospital deployments are byte-identical to v5 (verified on NWICU hemoglobin@12h).

preconditions_before_any_label_is_read: data access approved under PhysioNet credentialing and each database's terms

an extractor per database producing transitions in the MIMIC-IV contract: 6h anchor step, 6h look-back, label = nearest measurement within min(2, h/2) hours of anchor + h, 72h episode cap, plausibility cleaning as in mimiciv_observation_transition_extract.py

variable mapping declared from the data dictionary only, following the harmonized definitions: glucose = chemistry laboratory glucose; point-of-care glucose -> glucose_poc; blood-gas glucose -> glucose_bg; nurse-validated vital signs where the database distinguishes them; urine output interval-normalized to mL/hour; MAP = measured mean pressure

an addendum file recording the SHA-256 of each extractor and mapping file and the extraction outputs, written before the extracted labels are opened; before the addendum only support counts and timestamps may be inspected, never target values

commands.continuous: python3 site_adaptive_external_audit.py --database <SICdb|HiRID> --external-template <extracted {horizon} template> --protocol adaptive_model_lockbox_protocol_v4_20261020.json --output site_adaptive_lockbox_<database>_<date>.json (all other options at their defaults)
commands.emory_extraction: python3 emory_challenge2019_transition_extract.py --root ~/mimic/physionet.org/files/challenge-2019/1.0.0/training/training_setB --horizon-hours <h> --output emory_challenge2019_transitions_<h>h.parquet --report emory_challenge2019_transitions_<h>h.json for h in 1, 3, 6, 12, 24, 48

evaluation.cells: all 49 catalog cells; cells the site does not record are reported as not evaluable
evaluation.stream: the database is one site; stays in fixed random arrival order (seeded), chronological within a stay; outcome resolves at anchor + horizon; at most 60,000 rows per cell
evaluation.samples: 5 MIMIC training samples of 15,000 rows (sample 0 = original seed)
evaluation.gates: unchanged: point = patient-cluster paired bootstrap CI upper < 0 vs persistence and vs the recipe's comparator; interval = patient-equal and care-unit-equal whole-stream coverage in [0.87, 0.93], every care unit weighted equally (researcher decision 2026-10-19)

primary_endpoint: per database: number of evaluable continuous cells robust under point_and_dtaci_adaptive
secondary: robust counts under static v2 and the other adaptive configurations on the same streams
robust point counts; per-cell coverage, half-width and MAE relative to persistence
development_reference_caveat: in-sample: recipes and theta0 were selected on these databases; the leave-one-database-out interval estimate for theta0 was 93 vs 85 robust intervals
decision_rule: cells robust on at least two of SICdb, HiRID and Emory are independently replicated adaptive cells; robust on one = candidate. Emory counts as independent by researcher decision on 2026-10-20: the current deployment form never used it, although a separate earlier model line did (see prior_project_use); reports must state this. Any registry change requires the user's approval.
one_shot_rule: each database is scored once; only crashes may be fixed, without changing methods, gates or cohorts, and every fix is reported
refreeze_rule: if any hashed file changes before scoring, a new protocol version must be frozen before any label is read; site_adaptive_external_audit.py and multi_sample_external_audit.py refuse to score SICdb/HiRID when any hash differs
supersedes: adaptive_model_lockbox_protocol_v5_20261020.json (SICdb/HiRID never scored); re-frozen to add network sharing for multi-hospital deployments. Changed hashed files: site_adaptive_external_audit.py; added: site_adaptive_network_dev_20261020.json

emory_addendum.data_access: open access (PhysioNet Challenge 2019, ODC-By); no credentialing required
emory_addendum.inspected_before_freeze: Challenge web page and paper; file listing; column header; for 2,000 set-B files the magnitudes of non-target inputs only (Temp, FiO2, Calcium, Lactate, Magnesium, Phosphate, TroponinI, Unit1, Unit2, ICULOS, HospAdmTime). No target value (glucose, MAP, platelets, heart rate, hematocrit, hemoglobin, potassium, respiratory rate, creatinine, O2 saturation, bicarbonate, chloride, BUN) was read.
emory_addendum.extractor: emory_challenge2019_transition_extract.py (mapping and unit factors inside; hashed in frozen_code_sha256)
declared_differences: hourly bins: multiple measurements within an hour are their median; each row is timed at the end of its hour
LOINC codes for one parameter are merged by the Challenge (e.g. serum and arterial hemoglobin; MIMIC hemoglobin/hematocrit itemids also include blood gas)
glucose is the Challenge's serum glucose; whether point-of-care values were merged is not documented
absent: sodium and urine output (cells not evaluable), point-of-care and blood-gas glucose, treatments (treatment-context recipes fall back to the measurement-pure ridge)
care units: MICU / SICU / unknown from Unit1 and Unit2
one file = one ICU stay; no cross-stay patient identifier, so each stay is its own patient
Challenge selection: ICU patients curated for sepsis prediction (all ICU patients with the 40 variables, labelled by Sepsis-3; SepsisLabel is not used)
emory_addendum.extraction_output_hashes: to be recorded in an addendum file after extraction and before any label is opened
emory_addendum.data_location: ~/mimic/physionet.org/files/challenge-2019/1.0.0/training/training_setB (downloaded 2026-06-16); a fresh partial download on 2026-10-20 (~/Downloads/physionet-challenge-2019) matched it byte for byte on 3,000 compared files and is not used

scored_results.Emory: scored once under v5 on 2026-10-20 (site_adaptive_lockbox_Emory_20261020.json: 40/41 continuous, hypoxemia 2/2); remains valid under v6 because Emory is a single hospital and the single-hospital path is unchanged. Not to be re-scored.
